handoff.objective: Run the five preregistered hardening arms, reusing the BATCH-fe0bdc producer line where the control says so (its src/ and KAT pins are your lineage; disclose reuse): (J4, LOAD-BEARING) one r=6 RANDOM-BIJECTION arm at 2^30 -- same probe geometry and comparator, S-box replaced by a freshly drawn random bijection on 16 symbols (seed pinned in preregistration); preregistered expectation under the nonlinearity reading: DEAD/absence like AES at r=6; an ALIVE reading kills the 'nonlinearity-driven' wording and must be reported as such. (J3) second-seed/key rerun of the r=6 affine arm from BATCH-fe0bdc (~49 s), preregistered expectation: hits = 2^30 (T=0), W=3 on 100% nontrivial, as the identity law is deterministic. (J2) keyed bridge cells at r in {3, 7} (500 trials each), preregistered expectation: identity law + W law on 100%. (J1) census extension r = 11..16 over the same frozen cell set (pure GF(2) algebra) plus one r = 16 keyed cell (500 trials), preregistered expectation: flat per the r-free derivation and the identity law at the keyed cell. (GUARD) identity-law bridge on the dead keyed murmur3-fmix64 Feistel substitute of EV-AES-dec938 (500 trials), preregistered expectation: the identity law FAILS there (premise D-affine does not hold for the substitute), empirically sealing the proves-too-much non-transfer that was derivation-only. Report each arm against its preregistered expectation and name the verdict-level consequence of each outcome.
handoff.uncertainty_reduced: Whether the four overclaim joints of EV-AES-ec53f1 (J1-J4) survive their cheapest named controls, and whether the proves-too-much non-transfer holds empirically.
